description.value: Attempt a Perception or Occultism check (your choice) against the target's Will DC. On a success, you learn its Anchor and can target it with Break the Anchor for the rest of the encounter. Without a Name, Break the Anchor doesn't work. No daily limit — but a failed attempt tips the target off that you're looking.

target.value: 1 hostile spirit or ghost-machine you can perceive

cinderfall.incomplete: This is the foundational mechanic that marks a specific perceived creature as 'Named' after a successful check, and it has no real pf2e analog: no rule element marks a specific creature with a persistent custom tag after a check success without a companion Effect item applied directly to that creature. The one real precedent for a comparable 'flag this specific foe' pattern, Warding Aggression (pf2e-source/packs/pf2e/spells/spells/rank-3/warding-aggression.json), does exactly that via a second, linked Spell Effect item (Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Spell Effect: Warding Aggression), not a field on the spell itself. Building an equivalent companion effect record for 'Named' is out of scope for this single-file rule-element pass. This also explains why anchor-break, chain-reaction, chalk-and-iron, hunters-ledger, and mass-exorcism can't be built: they all key off 'Named,' which has no rule-element representation to extend.
